text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on February 26 in history.
1531 - Between 20,000 and 30,000 people died in an earthquake in Lisbon.
1797 - The Bank of England issued one pound notes for the first time.
1802 - Victor Hugo, French poet and novelist, born. Leader of the French Romantic movement, his greatest novel "Les Miserables", was published in 1862.
1808 - Honore Daumier, French caricaturist and painter, born. He was best known for his cartoons and drawings satirising 19th-century politics and society.
1832 - The Polish constitution was abolished and replaced by one imposed by Tsar Nicholas I.
1834 - Alois Senefelder, German inventor of lithography, died.
1839 - In Britain, the first Grand National horse race was run.
1846 - Buffalo Bill, American frontiersman and showman, born as William Frederick Cody.
1848 - The Second French Republic was proclaimed.
1852 - The British troop ship Birkenhead sank off Simon's Bay, South Africa, with the loss of 485 lives.
1857 - Emile Coue, French psychologist and pioneer of "Auto-suggestion", born. His system was expressed in the formula "Every day, in every way, I am becoming better"
1885 - The Congress of Berlin, hosted by Otto von Bismarck and attended by 15 nations, agreed on the partition of Central and East Africa.
1901 - The leaders of the Boxer Rebellion in China, Chi-hsui and Hsu Cheng-yu, were beheaded in public.
1903 - Richard Gatling, American inventor of the cylinder gun that bears his name, died.
1903 - Orde Wingate, British general who led his forces against the Japanese in Burma in World War Two, born in India.
1916 - Jackie Gleason, American comedian and actor, born.
1916 - The Germans sunk the French transport ship Provence II, killing 930.
1928 - Fats Domino, U.S. singer and pianist notably of "Ain't That a Shame" and "Blueberry Hill", born.
1932 - Johnny Cash, U.S. country singer, born.
1935 - RADAR (Radio Detection and Ranging) was first demonstrated by Robert Watson-Watt.
1936 - In Germany, Adolf Hitler opened the first factory for the production of the "People's Car", the Volkswagen, in Saxony.
1952 - Winston Churchill announced that Britain had produced its own atomic bomb and would be testing it in Australia.
1961 - Prince Hassan acceded to the throne of Morocco as King Hassan II, following the sudden death of his father Mohammed V.
1969 - Levi Eshkol, Israeli prime minister since 1963, died.
1976 - Spain handed over the Western Sahara to Morocco and Mauritania.
1980 - Egypt and Israel established diplomatic relations, marking the end of 30 years of war between the two.
1981 - Three Anglican missionaries detained in Iran since August 1980 were released.
1984 - The last American marines in the multinational peacekeeping force in Lebanon left Beirut.
1990 - The Soviet Union agreed to withdraw all its 73,500 troops from Czechoslovakia by July, 1991.
1993 - A bomb exploded at the World Trade Centre in New York. The blast, the worst terrorist attack to date on American soil, killed six people and injured more than 1,000.

1994 - Sworn enemies of Russian President Boris Yeltsin walked free from jail under a parliamentary amnesty. They included former vice-president Alexander Rutskoi, and the ex-chairman of the disbanded parliament, Ruslan Khasbulatov.
1995 - The London finance house of Barings collapsed after losses run up in Singapore by trader Nick Leeson.
